Hunt, the nation’s largest intermodal service operator, told regulators last week that it opposes the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger, believing it would likely provide “more harm than benefit” for J.B. Hunt customers. In Nov. 18 comments to the Surface Transportation Board, the trucking and freight brokerage company argued that the merger application’s focus on the benefits of single-line service and its projection of 2.1 million road-to-rail conversions “are not consistent with J.B. Hunt’s real-world experience in moving approximately 2.25 million intermodal loads by rail annually.” The application also provides no assurances that the projected benefits of the merger would be passed on to shippers, the company says, or that UP and NS would be held accountable if promised service levels are not achieved. candidates.excerpt: BROUSSARD, La. — Amtrak’s Sunset Limited derailed today (Sunday, Nov. 22) in Broussard after a grade crossing collision with a truck carrying a bulldozer, KSLA-TV reports. An Amtrak statement said the derailment occurred about 6:15 p.m. and that the train’s locomotives and two baggage cars derailed, but all passenger cars remained upright. There were 95 passengers on board; bus transportation will be provided to their destination. Acadian Ambulance said in a Facebook post that it sent 12 ambulances to the scene and transported four patients to the hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. Seven ambulance crews remained at the scene to triage and treat other passengers. The Lafayette Fire Department said in a later Facebook post that at least five people had suffered minor injuries. candidates.title: Equinor and NCL extend low-carbon marine fuel agreement
candidates.excerpt: Equinor and North Sea Container Line (NCL) have extended their collaboration on low-carbon marine fuels into 2027. Under the extended agreement, Equinor will continue supplying low-carbon bunker fuel from its Tjeldbergodden industrial plant in Norway to NCL’s dual-fuel methanol container vessels, NCL Vestland and NCL Nordland. The companies began working together during 2026, establishing a direct supply chain between the fuel production facility and NCL’s container shipping operations. Biomethanol production at Tjeldbergodden Equinor’s Tjeldbergodden plant is certified to produce biomethanol using mass-balanced biomethane supplied by European Union producers through the interconnected European gas grid. The arrangement allows NCL’s two vessels to continue using lower-carbon fuel while operating along the Norwegian coastline. candidates.title: Samudera and CONCOR sign agency agreement for EXIM cargo
candidates.excerpt: Samudera has signed an agency agreement with Container Corporation of India Ltd (CONCOR) aimed at improving coordination between inland logistics and international shipping services. The agreement was formalised at CONCOR’s head office in New Delhi on 26 October 2026. Under the arrangement, the companies will support export-import cargo movements across markets including India, Thailand, Malaysia, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, the United Arab Emirates and Indonesia. The cooperation combines CONCOR’s inland logistics capabilities with Samudera’s established regional shipping network. It is also expected to provide a basis for exploring additional markets and expanding CONCOR’s overseas reach. Samudera and CONCOR said they intend to expand shipping activities and provide customers with more integrated logistics solutions. The announcement does not specify any new liner service, port rotation, implementation schedule or financial terms associated with the agreement.

The Mumbai-listed owner has issued tenders covering eight 88,000 cu m very large gas carriers (VLGCs), six 18,000 teu containerships, up to six 8,000 teu boxships and two 155,000 dwt suezmax tankers. The vessels are being sought for a proposed joint venture involving state-owned energy companies Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum. The gas carrier programme comes with a significant domestic construction requirement. candidates.excerpt: Semaf calls off Renfe drivers’ strike after deal with Spanish ministry The Spanish train drivers’ union Semaf has called off the Renfe strike planned for Monday 23 November, which would also have hit Renfe Mercancías freight trains. The union reached a safety agreement with the Spanish Ministry of Transport on 20 November. Semaf was the last union still maintaining the strike call, as the other Renfe and Adif unions had reportedly already ended their protests. The 23 November stoppage itself replaced an earlier strike day, which Semaf postponed after the government approved extra safety measures. The breakthrough came with a new protocol for adverse weather, based on thresholds from forecasts by the Spanish State Meteorological Agency (Aemet). Semaf also secured new rules for faults in the LZB and ERTMS signalling systems, daily publication of temporary speed restrictions and earlier retirement for rail staff. The global tram and light rail vehicle market is entering a second major renewal wave. The first large-scale generation of low-floor vehicles was introduced mainly during the 1990s and early 2000s; many of these fleets are now 20 to 30 years old and approaching life expiry. Europe remains the core market, but demand is increasingly spreading to Latin America, the Middle East, Asia-Pacific and North America. candidates.excerpt: U.S. rail traffic rose 7.3% in the week ending November 14, 2026, compared with the same week last year, as double-digit intermodal growth outpaced gains in conventional carload shipments, according to the Association of American Railroads. Intermodal volume increased 10.7% year over year, while total carloads rose 3.3%, AAR said in a weekly update. Eight of the 10 carload commodity groups recorded gains. Motor vehicles and parts posted the strongest percentage increase among carload categories, rising 16.2%. Forest products followed with a 14% gain, while metallic ores and metals increased 10.7% and petroleum and petroleum products advanced 10.3%. The remaining categories posting increases were farm products excluding grain, and food, up 3.1%; chemicals, up 2.3%; nonmetallic minerals, up 2.1%; and coal, up 0.9%. Grain shipments fell 4.7%. candidates.title: Private credit gains ground in Asia amid AI boom
candidates.excerpt: Private credit gains ground in Asia amid AI boom Private credit is gaining ground in Asia as demand for flexible capital grows and the AI boom needs funding, according to KKR. Asia has historically relied on banks for credit, and they still provide 88 per cent of the region’s debt capital, compared with 50 per cent in Europe and just 31 per cent in the US. However, forces reshaping Japan and driving investment in AI infrastructure are starting to change this, KKR said in a recent blog post. In the US and Europe, regulators have made banks retrench, but that is not happening in Asia. Instead, private credit is in demand across the region because it offers flexible capital alongside banks that remain deeply embedded in corporate financing. KKR argued that Asian banks provide cheap but inflexible capital, and that private credit was plugging this gap. AAR Reports Weekly Rail Traffic for the Week Ending November 14, 2026
candidates.excerpt: The Association of American Railroads (AAR) has reported U.S. rail traffic for the week ending November 14, 2026. For this week, total U.S. weekly rail traffic was 529,919 carloads and intermodal units, up 7.3 percent compared with the same week last year. Total carloads for the week ending November 14 were 230,260 carloads, up 3.3 percent compared with the same week in 2025, while U.S. weekly intermodal volume was 299,659 containers and trailers, up 10.7 percent compared to 2025. Eight of the 10 carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They included motor vehicles and parts, up 2,182 carloads, to 15,691; metallic ores and metals, up 1,979 carloads, to 20,470; and petroleum and petroleum products, up 1,063 carloads, to 11,362. Commodity groups that posted decreases compared with the same week in 2025 were grain, down 1,205 carloads, to 24,396; and miscellaneous carloads, down 239 carloads, to 8,801. candidates.title: Domestically produced Russian high speed train to be tested in 2027
candidates.excerpt: Domestically produced Russian high speed train to be tested in 2027 RUSSIA: Ural Locomotives is advancing development of the prototype EVS360 Bely Krechet (White Gyrfalcon) high speed trainset, with Russian Railways expecting it to be delivered for testing during 2027. The Bely Krechet project being undertaken by Sinara Group’s Ural Locomotives subsidiary in partnership with mostly Russian suppliers covers the development and production of 43 eight-car trainsets for the planned Moskva – St Petersburg high speed line. Two prototype trainsets are to be produced ahead of the 41 production units, with deliveries scheduled for 2028-30. The EVS360 is intended for operation at up to 360 km/h, with a maximum design speed of 400 km/h. The eight-car train will accommodate approximately 454 passengers in four classes, with a bistro car also provided.
